arguments.context:
## Confirmed Knowledge:

1. **Project identified**: Tōrea (South Island Pied Oystercatcher) banding project in New Zealand — verified via https://shorebirds.org.nz/archives/11812
   - June 2021: 114 birds caught at Kuranui Bay, Thames (within 110-120 range ✓)
   - 22 birds fitted with GPS units (within 20-25 range ✓)
   - Two organizations manage data: Manaaki Whenua | Landcare Research (MWLR) and Department of Conservation (DOC)

2. **Bird banding system CONFIRMED**: 
   - From shorebirds.org.nz/archives/11812: "You can enter your sightings directly into the Department of Conservation FALCON Bird Banding system."
   - Full form: FALCON = File Upload, Accessibility, Locality (mapping), Certification, Open-Source and Notification (communication)
   - The system went live in August 2020

3. **Movie character connection**: PMN Issue 121 has article "A SIPO called ET calls home" — E.T. from 1982 movie connected to the South Island Pied Oystercatcher (SIPO) project. This confirms the "band with name of a character from a movie released in 1982" criterion.

## Answer Status: HIGH CONFIDENCE (VERIFIED)
The question asks: "Please provide the name of the bird banding system used by this specific project in 2021."
All criteria match perfectly:
- 110-120 birds caught: 114 ✓
- 20-25 tracking devices: 22 ✓
- Band with 1982 movie character (E.T.): Confirmed via PMN Issue 121 ✓
- Bird banding system name: **FALCON** ✓

No further verification needed. Ready to finish.
